row.scim_price_text: Advanced: from $10.83/mo billed annually ($13 monthly) at 10K occurrences/mo, usage-based
row.team_price_text: Essentials: from $7.50/mo billed annually ($9 monthly) at 10K occurrences/mo, usage-based
row.evidence: Rollbar's pricing page lists SAML SSO and SCIM User provisioning only on Advanced and Enterprise, and the machine-readable pricing page says Advanced includes "SCIM".
row.notes: Unchanged status from June (gated, SCIM on Advanced). Pricing is usage-based on monthly error occurrences with unlimited users ('Rollbar never charges per seat'), so per-user prices and the multiplier are null; June's 2.1x multiplier came from event-tier prices, not per-user prices, and is dropped. The price ladder now starts at 10K occurrences/mo: Essentials $7.50/mo and Advanced $10.83/mo billed annually ($9/$13 monthly); at 25K occurrences the June figures still hold (Essentials $15.83, Advanced $32.50 annual). SAML SSO is also Advanced+. Rollbar's Okta guide and Microsoft's Entra tutorial still say provisioning is Enterprise-only, which conflicts with the pricing page. SCIM base URL, version, attributes and deprovision behaviour are not in Rollbar's docs. Account-level REST API (users, teams, invites) on all plans; audit controls are Enterprise, no audit-log API documented.

auth.token_source: Account Settings > Account Access Tokens (token with SCIM scope); IdP guides say copy the access token from Settings > Identity Providers > Provisioning Options

deprovision.notes: Rollbar never charges per seat, so seat freeing does not apply. Rollbar's OneLogin guide tells admins to pick Delete as the OneLogin deprovision action; Rollbar does not document what its SCIM endpoint does on deprovision.

roles.how: Pushed IdP groups become Rollbar teams; team access levels (standard/light/view) are set via the REST API, not documented for SCIM.

limitations.text: SCIM must be enabled for the account by Rollbar (contact sales/support) before the Provisioning Options section appears.
Users cannot be removed from provisioned teams in Rollbar; membership is controlled only by IdP group membership.
SAML must be configured before the provisioning section is shown.

scim.notes: Rollbar's pricing page and machine-readable pricing page put SCIM on Advanced; its older Okta guide and Microsoft's Entra tutorial still say Enterprise. Rollbar docs do not publish the SCIM base URL or SCIM version.

auth.notes: Account access token passed in the X-Rollbar-Access-Token header; account tokens have read and write scopes (plus a SCIM scope for provisioning).

capabilities.notes: Users are added by inviting them to teams; removing a user from all teams removes them from the account (delete_user = remove from account). Roles are team access levels (standard/light/view) set when creating a team.

endpoints.purpose: List all users who are members of an account
Check if a user is assigned to a team
Remove a user from a team (removal from all teams removes the user from the account)
Invite an email address to a team

webhooks_user_events.notes: Webhook events are item, occurrence and deploy events only.

rate_limits.text: API returns 429 Too Many Requests when rate limiting is enabled for the access token; numeric API limits not documented.

okta.notes: OIN app 'Rollbar': SAML, SWA and SCIM; provisioning Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking are checked on the OIN page.

entra.notes: Microsoft's tutorial maps userName, externalId, active, name.familyName, name.givenName, emails[type eq "work"] and group displayName, externalId, members; it says the Rollbar tenant needs an Enterprise Plan.

google.notes: Google's guide requires SSO first and asks admins to contact Rollbar support to enable provisioning.

onelogin.notes: From Rollbar's own OneLogin guide (catalogue app 'SAML 2.0 - user provisioning'); OneLogin catalogue page not checked (bot-blocked).

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud's Rollbar guide covers SAML SSO only; no SCIM section.

fallbacks.other_sync: Email-domain safelist lets verified users join the account (not directory sync)

conflicts.text: Rollbar's pricing page and machine-readable pricing page put SCIM on Advanced, but Rollbar's Okta guide says provisioning is on enterprise plans only and Microsoft's Entra tutorial requires an Enterprise Plan. The pricing page is used for the plan.
Rollbar's SCIM page says to create an Account Access Token with SCIM scope, while its Okta and OneLogin guides say to copy the access token from Identity Providers > Provisioning Options.

open_questions: SCIM base URL and SCIM version are not documented by Rollbar.
Rollbar does not document SCIM deprovision behaviour (deactivate vs remove), user attributes, filtering, pagination or rate limits for SCIM.
Whether SCIM is self-serve on Advanced or still needs sales/support enablement (older guides say contact sales).
No audit-log API is documented despite Enterprise 'Audit controls'.
